attacks.claim: Zero-config auto-loading executes any package in node_modules with the `tasq-plugin` keyword, with no allowlist or consent. Any transitive dependency (or a typosquat or compromised package) can add the keyword and gain code execution in every tasq invocation, including git pre-commit hooks, CI (with secrets) and editors. This is a supply-chain escalation that the 'no postinstall scripts' claim does not address.
attacks.evidence: "Any installed package with the `tasq-plugin` keyword is picked up automatically." / "loads the ones whose `keywords` include `tasq-plugin`"

attacks.claim: Discovery globs `**/node_modules/**/package.json` and parses every package.json on every invocation, including `--version`, with no caching. Cost scales with installed package count, so large monorepos will be slower still. The 180k weekly downloads include repos bigger than the 2,430-package reference.
attacks.evidence: glob("**/node_modules/**/package.json", { cwd: root }) ... "On every invocation (`tasq run`, `tasq lint-staged`, `tasq watch` restarts, `tasq list`)"

attacks.claim: Perf claim is contradicted by the artifact's own numbers. Discovery adds ~1.8s per invocation (cache-hit build goes 0.21s to 2.02s, `--version` 0.11s to 1.94s), which is about a 10x regression on the cached path. The 'under 50 ms of task time' highlight is misleading because wall-clock is 2s. 'Negligible' and 'overall build time improves' hold only for cold builds, and even there the gain is 2.6s, not clearly attributable to the cache.
attacks.evidence: "`tasq run build` (cache hit) | 0.21 s | 2.02 s" vs "Discovery is a fixed per-invocation cost and becomes negligible"

attacks.claim: The pre-commit hook path (`tasq lint-staged`) goes from 0.38s to 2.31s (~6x) on every commit, and editor integrations pay ~2s per call. This is a major friction regression on the documented recommended usage and is not listed in the breaking changes or mitigated, for example by a disable flag or a plugin manifest cache.
attacks.evidence: "`tasq lint-staged` (3 staged files) | 0.38 s | 2.31 s"; Context: docs recommend lint-staged in pre-commit hooks

attacks.claim: Glob over `**/node_modules/**` will match nested and duplicated package.json files, including fixtures and test files inside packages, so the same plugin can be found multiple times at different versions. There is no dedupe or version resolution. Discovery before arg parsing also means a malformed or throwing package.json crashes every command, including `--version`. The code has no try/catch around JSON.parse.
attacks.evidence: JSON.parse(await readFile(join(root, pkgJson), "utf8")) with no error handling; found.push with no dedupe

attacks.claim: The plugin-array change silently breaks existing setups. The `plugins` array is ignored and migrate installs nothing, so users who listed plugins explicitly lose them, or load different ones, with no warning. Users who explicitly excluded a plugin by not listing it now get it loaded. The rollback plan also ignores that users on `^2` ranges are unaffected but users who have already upgraded and migrated (ESM conversion, config rewrite) cannot be reverted by a dist-tag flip.
attacks.evidence: "`plugins` array in config ignored | Auto-discovery replaces it; `tasq-migrate` removes the array and installs nothing new"; "re-point `latest` to `2.9.4`"

attacks.claim: The staged rollout is undermined: the blog post and Discord announcement go live at publish while the version is only on `next`, so users are directed to a version that `npm i tasq` does not install. The 7-day no-P1 gate has no defined monitoring or P1 criteria. The rollback of `latest` does not help users who pinned 3.0.0 from `next`.
attacks.evidence: "Publish `3.0.0` under `next` dist-tag; promote to `latest` after 7 days" vs "Blog post and changelog go live at publish"

attacks.claim: The plugin smoke test covers the top 15 plugins only for loading, not for a malicious or hostile node_modules layout, performance in large trees, or non-hoisted pnpm layouts. The migrate test sample of 40 repos is small relative to the user base.
attacks.evidence: "Smoke test of top 15 community plugins under auto-discovery: all load and register subcommands."

attacks.claim: There is no mention of how the new ESM-only change and the plugin-loading behavior are documented in a security advisory or opt-out. Nothing here indicates a license or compliance problem.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: security documentation for auto-loaded code execution
